channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: In View 2027 · The Art Center Highland Park
item.description: The Art Center's annual members-and-faculty show in Highland Park, open to any subject, with photography first on its accepted-media list. Up to three works may be submitted but only one is hung, for a six-week run with a free public reception on 15 January. Work should be for sale and the gallery takes 35%. — Deadline: November 28, 2026. Fee: Free (membership required: $55–$105/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Alan Hagman Photojournalism Grant · National Press Photographers Foundation
item.description: A $6,000 grant for professional photojournalists authorized to work in the US or its territories, for underreported stories on human rights, the environment or other pressing social topics; a panel of photojournalism peers judges storytelling, sequencing and ethics. Payment is $5,000 on award and $1,000 on delivery of 25 captioned images within 18 months. The page's status chip reads Closed; its own prose and the live Picter portal run entries to 14 December. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $6,000.

item.title: The natural and the artificial · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group show at PH21's Barcelona gallery on the continuum between the organic and the designed — tamed gardens, abandoned spaces reclaimed by nature, and the frictions where the two meet. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over, 3 to 15 images submitted by email. Selected photographers pay a €45–€125 print and installation fee. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: €25–€45 early bird, then €30–€50; €15–€20 concession. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Winter Mountains
item.description: Outdoor Photography's monthly reader competition takes winter mountains as the theme for issue OP 336. Entrants send up to five images, each with a caption of up to 75 words and the full technical details in the magazine's stated order. Open to readers aged 18 or over, and uploads run through Google Drive, so a Google account is needed. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £159 gear + Publication.

item.title: 2027 Supporting Neurodivergent Creatives · Rotary Club of San Jose
item.description: The Rotary Club of San Jose's grant for neurodivergent artists aged 16 to 25 who live or work in the nine-county Bay Area, with photography explicitly among the eligible forms. Six artists each receive $2,500, and recipients must attend the May 2027 awards ceremony in downtown San Jose in person. — Deadline: February 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 grant.

item.title: Fine Art Awards 2026 · Dodho Magazine
item.description: Dodho Magazine's fine art competition, open worldwide, selects 100 finalists for a 30×30 cm printed annual edition. First, second and third prizes plus two honorable mentions receive a certificate and editorial visibility, and the overall winner is named Photographer of the Year; there is no cash prize. Entry is by paid image pack of three, six or twelve photographs, with VAT added for European entrants. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: €30 (3) / €45 (6) / €60 (12). Prize: Publication + Certificate.

item.title: HOME · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on the theme of home, open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, photography included. Every accepted work is shown in the online gallery; Best of Show wins $750 and two Director's Choice awards $250 each. AI-generated work is not accepted, and work shown in an earlier Art Fluent exhibit cannot be re-entered. — Deadline: February 19, 2027. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $750 + 2×$250.

item.title: PROUD+ 2027 · The Studio Door
item.description: The Studio Door in San Diego holds its tenth PROUD+ exhibition of work by LGBTQ+ artists from 25 June to 6 August 2027, juried by Xiangqi Chen of OUT Museum. Three artists receive a $100 Juror's Award, and all selected work appears in the catalogue. All work must be for sale at 50% commission, and international artists can join the online exhibition only. — Deadline: May 8, 2027. Fee: $35 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3). Prize: $100 awards + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Art of Possibilities Art Show & Sale 2027 · Allina Health Foundation
item.description: The 64th annual juried show for artists with disabilities, at the Courage Kenny Rehabilitation Institute in Minneapolis from 3 June to 9 July 2027, with Photography as one of six categories. Cash awards go to each category and a Best of Show, and artists keep 100% of sales. All work must be for sale; AI-generated work is not accepted. — Deadline: March 15, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Cash awards.

item.title: The Crow Show 2027 · The Studio Door
item.description:
The thirteenth annual national juried exhibition at The Studio Door, the gay-owned and operated gallery Patric Stillman founded in San Diego in 2014, celebrating the crow. The gallery's framing is that the crow has long been a symbol of mystery, transformation and intelligence across cultures, and artists are invited to explore its many faces, whether rooted in reality or soaring through fantasy: creative interpretations of black birds, ravens and other Corvus species are welcome. The call opened 15 November 2026 and the exhibition runs 19 February – 2 April 2027, with two public receptions, on 20 February and 27 March. Walkthrough videos of past editions are on the gallery's YouTube channel.
Each artist may enter up to three works, at $35 for the first and $5 for each additional entry. Submission is through CaFE: one to three JPEGs, at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side and under 5 MB. The accepted media are painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art, artist books and sculpture, with oversized jewellery that can be presented as fine art also eligible; performance art is not accepted, and video, film, installation or anything needing mains power requires gallery approval before submission. Framed two-dimensional work must use plexiglass rather than glass because of shipping and may not exceed 60 inches high by 40 inches wide including the frame; sculpture must fit through an average doorway and stay under eight feet. Glass and ceramic works are accepted only if hand-delivered. Patric Stillman is the sole juror; he served on the jury of the Oceanside Museum of Art's 2025 Biennial and writes a monthly arts column for The WORD San Diego.
Three artists each receive a $100 Juror's Award for imaginative and compelling interpretations of the theme, judged on originality, execution, emotional impact and interpretation. The juror selects works for the physical gallery and further works for an online gallery, and applicants choose which they want to be considered for; online-only selections are equally eligible for Best in Show. The gallery calls this a national exhibition based in the United States, and because of shipping costs, tariffs and customs, international artists may take part in the online exhibition only, with international sales handled by the gallery. All selected work, in gallery or online, appears in the exhibition catalogue, available online and print-on-demand. Jury review runs 17–21 January with notification on 22 January 2027. All work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining 50 per cent and commission cheques mailed within 30 days of closing; artists cover shipping and supply prepaid return labels. — Deadline: January 16, 2027. Fee: $35 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3). Prize: $100 awards + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: GRANDEUR OF COLOR · MVA Gallery
item.description:
MVA Gallery, a commercial gallery in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, runs a rolling programme of themed national group shows, and this one takes colour as its subject. The gallery's framing is that colour is everywhere and exerts a powerful influence on perception, emotion and behaviour, and that an artist's use of it is personal — intellectual or intuitive, purposeful or accidental, traditional or experimental. Some artists depict the perceived relationship between colours and objects faithfully; others inhabit a subjective universe where colour is relative, transferring shapes and transforming objects to reconstruct reality. Work may be realistic or imaginary, representational or abstract, with no restrictions on subject matter or style. The show occupies both of the gallery's exhibition rooms, 5–30 May 2027, with accepted work due at the gallery by 30 April 2027.
The gallery accepts painting, watercolour, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, ink, sculpture, fibre, drawing and photography, and states that all photographic processes are welcome. Photographs should be framed for a traditional presentation, with black or white frames preferred and white or off-white mats where used, though other mounting is considered and exceptions are made. There is no cut-off date for when the work was made. Work must not exceed 48 inches framed on the longest side or 50 lbs, must carry a stretched wire for hanging, and must not have been shown at MVA before. Entry is $35 for three different images and $5 for each additional file up to a maximum of nine; submission runs through CaFE only. Images must be JPEG, under 5 MB and at least 1,200 pixels on the longest side. Work may be offered for sale, with 70 per cent of any sale price going to the artist and 30 per cent to the gallery, and artists pay shipping and insurance both ways and must enclose a prepaid UPS or FedEx return label. A small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers, curators and academics reviews the work, and its decisions are final.
Three awards are in play. An Art of Distinction award selects one artist, photographer or sculptor for a featured show in the gallery's Exhibition Room Two at a future date. The Director's Choice Award is $200, granted at the executive director's discretion. The annual Grand Prize goes to one artist chosen from everyone exhibited at MVA across the calendar year, who is offered an exhibition opportunity in New York City. Artists in a further category are granted free submission to a future MVA exhibition. Notification is by email on or about 4 March 2027, with separate messages for invited and not-invited entries and no acknowledgement of applications before then. The call is national: artists must be 18 or older and current residents of the United States. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: REFLECTIONS · Kunsthalle Burkamp
item.description:
Kunsthalle Burkamp in Haltern am See is assembling a group exhibition on the theme REFLECTIONS, planned for 2 May to 18 July 2027 with a vernissage. The theme spans reflection as an optical phenomenon and reflection as inner, mental movement: mirrorings on shimmering materials, water, glass, light and shadow, and images caught between visibility, likeness and illusion — and also RE-FLECTIONS as echo, the return of memories, emotions and historical traces that change in the retelling. The building is a former Haltern glassworks, and the call makes a point of that history: glass, both transparent and reflective, is meant to carry particular weight in the show.
The call is open to artists of all ages; no particular training or exhibition record is required. Media named as welcome include painting, drawing, sculpture and photography, as well as other forms suited to the spaces, but large-format installations, film and elaborate projections cannot be realised for technical reasons. Both existing works and concepts for new production may be submitted. Each application may carry 1 to 10 works. Selection is made by the Kunsthalle's curatorial team, and selected artists are contacted around the turn of the year 2026/27.
There is no application fee. Artists who are selected pay a participation fee towards the exhibition's costs, expected to be €150–€350 depending on how much external funding the Kunsthalle secures, with the exact figure given on acceptance. Artists deliver their work to Haltern am See themselves; installation and deinstallation are handled by the Kunsthalle team or jointly with the artist, and the Kunsthalle organises sales. Material needed for presentation — plinths, framing for photographs — is the artist's to provide after consultation.
Applications go by email as a single PDF containing a statement on the work and its relation to the theme (max. one A4 page), images with title, year, medium and dimensions, a short self-introduction for artists new to the Kunsthalle, and any special technical requirements. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: Free (€150–€350 participation fee if selected). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Open Call for Exhibitions 2027 · Valokuvakeskus Peri
item.description:
Valokuvakeskus Peri (Photographic Centre Peri) is one of Finland's seven regional photography centres, working in photography and lens-based contemporary art from the Kilta Gallery in Art House Turku, a former fire station at Nunnankatu 4. It is now seeking exhibition proposals for its 2027 programme from artists, collectives and curators working professionally in those fields, and says it particularly wants to highlight the work of underrepresented artists and topics that have had little or no attention in the Finnish art field.
The economics are stated plainly and in the artist's favour: Peri does not charge a gallery rental fee, and it pays an exhibition fee to every exhibitor. The number of shows is deliberately limited so that each artist can be paid properly — four exhibition periods of roughly seven weeks, with one or two exhibitions selected for each, the first opening to the public on 7 May 2027. Artists are part of the working community during installation and deinstallation, and the centre provides production support.
The gallery is three rooms totalling 228.5 m² (107, 66 and 55.5 m², the last able to be darkened); partition walls take works almost anywhere, the ceiling has regular bolt points, and the street-facing stone window walls cannot be hung. Peri also says it wants to reduce unpaid application work: a proposal does not need to be production-ready, and its degree of finish is not itself a selection criterion.
Proposals go through an online form with a PDF of the proposal and work samples (under 50 MiB) plus a CV. The jury is exhibition curator Maria Huokkola, photographic artist Emma Sarpaniemi and senior university lecturer in photography and author Hanna Weselius; the director takes part in the process to check each proposal is feasible with Peri's resources, and jury members declare conflicts of interest and stand aside on those proposals. The director also keeps open telephone hours during the application period, 10:00–12:00 on Friday 20 November 2026. — Deadline: December 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Artist fee.

item.title: Studio Residency Stipend — Summer 2027 · Bibliothek Andreas Züst
item.description:
The Bibliothek Andreas Züst is an art library housed in the Alpenhof, a panorama lodge at 1,110 m above the Rhine Valley in Oberegg, Appenzell Innerrhoden, built around the collection of the Swiss artist, photographer and natural scientist Andreas Züst. Once a year it offers a six-week work and living space, and the next residency runs 4 July – 15 August 2027.
The stipend is deliberately collaborative: it is open to duos and collectives of up to five people, both established teams and newly founded ones that want to try working together. The organiser's own information sheet lists the disciplines it covers — visual arts, literature, new media, music, theatre, design, architecture, film, photography, applied arts and art-related academic disciplines — and asks for projects that engage with the library as a whole or one of its sub-areas, in the tradition of libraries as places of knowledge. Applications from families and people with children are welcome.
Accommodation, food and use of the studio are free of charge, travel to and from the Alpenhof by public transport is covered, and each resident gets a Half-Fare card for the month; a separate request can be made for an additional living-cost subsidy of up to CHF 750. Accident insurance is the resident's own. Everyone has a private bedroom, though the information sheet notes that a work space outside the bedroom is not possible for every resident; the library and the rooms and niches around the house are open for concentrated work. Life on site is self-organised, cooking and cleaning included — residents take turns making the shared dinner from a stocked kitchen. A maximum of ten stipendiaries is taken in total. Applicants from outside Switzerland need an entry permit, and the call is aimed at people resident in Europe.
Application is by email as a single PDF of no more than 7 MB, containing the completed application form, a project description (max. 1 A4 page), documentation of previous projects (max. 5 pages), a CV for each collaborator (max. 1 page each) and a page on the motivation and way of working together as a collective. Residents are chosen by a panel of library representatives and one external member, announced by 31 January 2027; the panel gives no reasons for its decision. The programme is sponsored by Verein Ida, Zürich. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + CHF 750 subsidy.

item.title: London Showcase February 2027 · HUGE Gallery
item.description:
This call is for HUGE Gallery's London showcase at The Factory, 21–31 Shacklewell Lane, London E8, from 5 to 7 February 2027. HUGE Gallery runs three-day group showcases in several cities and describes itself as an open exhibition platform for emerging artists. The listing for this edition names its disciplines explicitly: painting, sculpture, photography, illustration, mixed media, digital art, installation, textiles and more. No previous exhibitions are required, selection depends on the work and its fit with the show, and artists do not need to live locally or attend in person.
Applying is free; places are paid for by the artists who are selected, and the price is the one thing this edition's card does not print. Every other city on the page names its fees — HUGE's other current London edition, running 27–29 November 2026, is £80 for a physical place, £45 small physical and £35–£50 digital, while Tokyo starts at £300 — and the site's chat panel states a site-wide floor of £50 for a digital place and £150 for a physical one. The FAQ says only that fees vary by show and format. Expect a charge somewhere in that span, named in writing when HUGE offers the place. A physical place means the work is presented in the venue according to the individual call's requirements; a digital place means on-screen and online presentation. Documentation and social features depend on the exhibition.
Applying starts with a mailing-list signup rather than a form: the "Apply Here" link goes to a Flodesk page on HUGE's own list (hosted under its billboardresidency account), which collects a name and email address and sends access to the application by email. That gate is also why no submission requirements are listed here: how many works may be entered, and in what format, is not visible until HUGE emails the form. — Deadline: January 23, 2027. Fee: Free (participation fee if selected, from £50). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Maternal and Infant Health Innovation Center — Art Purchase for Mercer County Artists · New Jersey State Council on the Arts
item.description: The State of New Jersey is buying already-finished two-dimensional work from Mercer County artists to hang in the Maternal and Infant Health Innovation Center, a newly built facility at 1 Pennington Avenue in Trenton's Capital Complex and the home of the New Jersey Maternal and Infant Health Innovation Authority — the first state authority in the country dedicated to maternal and infant health outcomes and to racial and ethnic disparities in care. Photography is one of five media named in the call and one of the five the community survey asked for, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking and mixed media; the survey also reported appetite for palettes from bold to muted, for work from abstract to representational, and most of all for images of people and cityscapes, with interest in landscapes, animals and work that reflects what the centre does. There is no preferred style. The total purchase budget is up to $50,000, spread across multiple artists, and no single piece may be priced above $1,000 all-inclusive — anything priced higher is not considered. Free to apply, up to four images of completed, ready-to-install work, framed and wired, fragile materials behind glass or plexiglas, nothing larger than 42 inches in any direction including the frame (a diptych or triptych counts as one work and must fit the same limit). Work that is political, violent or sexual is out, as the building is a public state office. An Art Selection Committee of community members, state workers and arts experts shortlists from the submitted images, then views the shortlisted works in person before deciding; not every shortlisted work is bought, and artists collect unsold work after the viewing. Statuses are communicated by the end of March 2027. Open to New Jersey residents 18 or older who live in Mercer County or keep a permanent studio address there; State of New Jersey employees are barred by statute. A Zoom project overview and Q&A runs on Friday 11 December 2026, 12-1pm, and written questions close 18 December 2026. — Deadline: January 7, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 purchase.

item.title: Re-Source · The HeArt Box
item.description: The HeArt Box, an artist-run contemporary gallery in downtown Flagstaff, Arizona, and the Azulita Project — a nonprofit working to prevent and reduce plastic waste — invite artists in all media, photography named among them, to a juried exhibition about where art materials come from and what they cost the world. Creative reuse, natural and regenerative materials, fiber, earth pigments and low-impact practices are welcome, but so is work made with acrylics, plastics and petroleum-based products by artists willing to question those choices: you do not have to use recycled or natural materials to take part, only to think critically about the materials you do use. Each submission carries a list of materials used and a 100-word statement on the artist's relationship to them, alongside an artist statement or bio and a portfolio link. Up to three pieces per artist, 1-3 JPEGs, $15 submission fee, which the gallery says goes to the costs of hosting and promoting the show. The gallery is small and work around 24 x 24 inches sits best, though all sizes are considered. Selection is on artistic quality, originality and thoughtful engagement with materials; notifications 8 March 2027, drop-off 8-11 April, exhibition 16 April - 30 May 2027 with a ticketed fundraising reception on 16 April and an Art Walk artist reception on 7 May. Work may be offered for sale and the gallery retains 50% commission, with a portion of proceeds going to the Azulita Project. Artists arrange and pay for shipping or deliver to the gallery at 17 N. San Francisco Street. — Deadline: February 15, 2027. Fee: $15 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Art Advocacy Project 2D (TAAP 2D) 2027 · City of Loveland Art in Public Places
item.description: The City of Loveland's Art in Public Places programme hangs a year-long, on-loan exhibition in the Central Galleria of the Loveland Public Library, and the 2027 call is open to Colorado artists working in any two-dimensional medium — the call names fiber, charcoal, mixed media and painting, and the prospectus deals with photography directly: selected work must stay up for the full year, but photographs that are part of a limited edition may be sold and the print replaced within the first six months of hanging. Selected artists are paid a $350 honorarium and may offer work for sale, though sales are not required; if a piece does sell, Art in Public Places retains 20% of the purchase value as commission. Since 2022 the programme has paired exhibiting artists with the Loveland Poet Laureate committee, so a selected artist may spend time talking through their work with a poet whose poem is then shown alongside it; selected artists should plan to attend the Artist Talk and Poetry Reading Reception on Saturday 27 March 2027. One entry per artist, free to apply, open to anyone 18 or older at any career stage. Work must be valued at $2,500 or less, no larger than 36 x 36 inches, professionally framed with protective glass where applicable and ready to hang on an art rail with D-rings fitted before delivery; the corridor is high-traffic, so fragile or unprotected work is unlikely to be selected. A jury panel of Art in Public Places representatives and citizen volunteers makes the selection. Contracts are signed by 5 March 2027, work is delivered to the library on 18 March 2027, and the display runs from late March 2027 to late February 2028. — Deadline: January 11, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $350 honorarium + Exhibition.

item.title: EWR Newark Liberty Airport Digital Art Exhibition 2027 · New Jersey State Council on the Arts
item.description: The Art of New Jersey is the annual digital exhibition inside the public art programme at Newark Liberty International Airport's new Terminal A, shown on the digital welcome banner spanning the departures area and rotated through large digital display units across the terminal for about a year. The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey's Art Advisory Council reviews submissions and selects roughly twenty artists; each selected artist receives a $1,000 stipend for the use of their work and retains copyright, and names and images are circulated through the Port Authority's, MANJ's and the State Arts Council's channels and a supporting website. Photography is explicitly in scope: the call asks for completed, two-dimensional, still work in digital form, either high-quality digital images of paintings, drawings, prints and photographs or work born digital, including digital photographs. Moving image, performance, new designs, tourism-style posters and sketches are not considered, and AI-generated work is excluded. Artists submit up to two previously completed works plus a short bio, a statement of any connection to Newark or Elizabeth, and a brief description of each piece; selected artists supply a PNG or JPG 1080 pixels high and are paid by direct bank deposit. Free to enter. Open to artists and artist teams 18 or older who are current residents of New Jersey — every team member must qualify — with priority to artists living in Newark and Elizabeth, where the airport sits; artists selected for the 2026 exhibition and submissions from artists' estates are not eligible. Notifications in spring 2027, exhibition opening in summer 2027. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Women Photography Awards 2026
item.description: An international single-image competition for photographers who self-identify as women, open worldwide to amateurs and professionals alike and judged anonymously across ten categories: Abstract, Architecture, Documentary, Fine-Art, Landscape, Open Theme, Pets, Portrait, Street and Wedding. The overall winner takes the title of Women Photographer of the Year with a €1,000 cash prize paid in euros, publication in the online winners' gallery, a feature in the awards' hardcover full-colour annual book and a winner's logo and certificate; honourable mentions and editors' picks get gallery publication, book inclusion and social features. One entry may be submitted into several categories at a discount, and entries are scored category by category, with the highest individual score taking the category. The jury is Kristina Varaksina, Foteini Zaglara and Emily Sims, all working photographers. The terms are unusually clear for a competition of this kind: copyright and intellectual property stay with the photographer at all times, every published image carries the photographer's credit, and usage extends only to the awards' own media partners. Judging is blind, so files must carry no signature, watermark, border or other identifying mark, and titles must not name the photographer. Winners supply a file of at least 3000px at 300dpi for the book, and the organisers reserve the right to ask finalists for the original RAW or unedited file to prove authorship and confirm the work was not generated using AI. Entrants must be 18 or over, hold sole copyright and have consent from identifiable subjects. Winners are announced five weeks after the deadline. — Deadline: November 18, 2026. Fee: €25 per single image + €15 each additional category. Prize: €1,000 + Book feature.

item.title: Flanelle Photography Awards 2026
item.description: The first annual awards from Flanelle, the independent Montreal fashion-photography magazine, aimed at "the images that stay with you" and open to photographers worldwide at any level, amateur or professional. Four categories: Women's Fashion and Men's Fashion (styled, concept-driven work for editorial or publication), Beauty (editorial beauty and make-up as the primary subject), and Emerging Photographer, reserved for photographers with less than two years' experience and open across the other three themes. A Photographer of the Year Grand Prix is drawn from all submissions with no separate entry. An entry is up to eight photographs submitted as a series, $25 per entry, and you may enter more than one category. The jury is named and sits outside the magazine for three of its four seats: Steven Branco (Editor-in-Chief, View the VIBE), make-up artist Marika D'auteuil (Makeup Artist of the Year at the Contessa Awards), Dan Blake (co-founder of the London College of Style, stylist with Vogue and GQ credits) and Flanelle's own founder and editor-in-chief Sarah-Eve Leduc; all entries are scored on creativity, technical quality, relevance to a fashion and editorial aesthetic, and emotional impact, with deliberation on 18–20 December. There is no cash prize. Each category winner is featured on the cover of an upcoming Flanelle print issue (the magazine values this at $800), receives a free year of a Kavyar Pro Biz account, a hard copy of the issue and a year in the Flanelle Directory, with a free year of Kavyar Pro for all credited team members — a stated total value over $1,600, most of it a publication credit and software rather than money. Entrants must be 18 or over and own the rights to everything submitted; images must be free of watermarks, borders or identifying text; children's fashion is not accepted; completely AI-generated images are not eligible. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $25 per entry (up to 8 photos). Prize: Cover publication + Kavyar Pro + Directory listing.

item.title: Communication Arts Photography Competition 2027
item.description: The 68th year of the photography competition run by Communication Arts, the Californian design and visual-communication journal whose annuals are a standing reference for art directors, designers and art buyers. An international jury of creative directors and photographers selects the winners, and every winning entry is published worldwide in the Communication Arts Photography Annual in print and digital editions and on commarts.com, with a contact index for the photographers represented — the point of the thing is to be found by people who commission work. There is no cash prize: each winner receives an Award of Excellence milled from solid aluminium plus printed certificates for all creative contributors. Nine categories are judged — Advertising, Books, Editorial, For Sale (posters, prints, greeting cards, licensing/stock, gallery and online-store sales), Institutional, Motion/Cinematography, Self-Promotion, Unpublished and Student Work — and the Unpublished category explicitly takes commissioned-but-unpublished, personal and experimental work, so this is not only for photographers with an ad-agency client list. Any photograph first published or produced between March 2026 and March 2027 is eligible, from any country; entry fees are $40 for a single image and $80 for a series of up to five in most categories ($90/$180 for time-based media, $20–$90 in the student categories), and descriptions in English matter to the judges. Entries registered after March 12 and up to March 26, 2027 cost $10 extra per submission. The competition states it will not accept AI text-to-image generated submissions. Accepted entrants are notified within two months of the final deadline. — Deadline: March 26, 2027. Fee: $40 single / $80 series; $90/$180 motion; $20–$90 student. Prize: Publication + Trophy.

item.title: In Good Company · The Studio Door
item.description: A new juried exhibition at The Studio Door, the gay-owned and operated gallery in San Diego, running August 13 – September 24, 2027, that asks San Diego County visual artists to portray each other: "Who should represent San Diego's working art community today?" Each selected artist makes a new portrait of another San Diego County artist, so the show adds up to a collective portrait of the region's art community seen one practitioner at a time. Portraiture here is not limited to painting or realism — photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art, artist books and sculpture, and expressive, symbolic and experimental interpretations are explicitly invited ("think beyond the familiar image of an artist holding a brush"). You apply with three to five existing images that show your approach to portraiture, not with a finished piece: either name three preferred subjects, with a note on why each artist's work deserves recognition, or ask the gallery to assign you one from a list built on recommendations from local art organisations and galleries. Selected artists are notified by April 9, 2027 with their confirmed subject, then have more than three months to make the work — progress images due July 1, final portrait and catalogue materials July 30, local delivery August 7. Participants are asked to keep their involvement confidential until opening night. Three artists each receive a $100 Juror's Award; all accepted portraits appear in an exhibition catalogue introducing the artists portrayed, and a copy is donated to the San Diego History Center as a record of this moment in the city's cultural life. Work must be original and available for sale, with sales split 50/50 with the gallery and commission cheques mailed within 30 days of the close. Performance art is not accepted; video, film, installation and anything needing external power require gallery approval first. Open to San Diego County artists only. — Deadline: April 3, 2027. Fee: $35 flat (3–5 artworks). Prize: $100 awards + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Interwoven Artist Residencies 2027 · Fabrica
item.description: Two fully funded month-long residencies across three partner organisations — Cow House Studios in Co. Wexford, Ireland (3–30 May 2027), Le Shed / Association Cybèle in Normandy, France (10 May–6 June 2027), and Fabrica in Brighton, UK (3–30 July 2027) — for contemporary visual artists willing to take their practice across borders. Interwoven starts from the textile legacies of the Norman era, the Bayeux Tapestry and the Sicilian Tristan quilts, read as evidence of inter-regional blending of technique, material, design and storytelling "through the creative skill of the female hand", and asks not for illustration of the past but for work that engages those European histories in ways relevant to now. The partners say they are particularly interested in artists bringing feminist, social or decolonial approaches. Each selected artist receives a €2,000 bursary for the month plus €500 for production expenses, accommodation and travel costs, desk space plus room to produce or test work, support from the host organisation, and a connection into the project's cross-border network of artists and organisations. Eligibility is geographic: the open call document limits the residencies to "visual artists based in France, the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Channel Islands, Flanders, Southern Italy (specifically Sicily, Puglia, Campania, Calabria), Norway and Denmark, with an interest in textile history, feminist histories, and/or with a textile-based practice". Applicants cannot apply to the residency in the country where they live, and must be able to stay up to 28 consecutive days. The call itself enumerates no media; photography is named in the Irish host's own provision - Cow House Studios lists a black-and-white darkroom printing 35mm up to 4x5in, film and digital cameras, studio lights and darkroom chemistry among its facilities, and its own open residency call names photographers among the practitioners encouraged to apply. The application is an expression of interest of up to 500 words about how the opportunity meets your practice rather than a defined project, a two-page statement and CV, and a five-page portfolio. Shortlisted artists are interviewed on 22 January 2027 and selections are announced by 5 February. The project forms part of the European Year of the Normans, initiated by the Région Normandie. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €2,000 bursary + €500 production + Residency.

item.title: 2026 AUTOMAT Open Call
item.description: The annual open call from AUTOMAT, an artist-run co-op gallery in Philadelphia's Crane Arts Building, for a group exhibition curated by the collective's own members. Open to emerging and mid-career artists working in any medium in the Philadelphia region. This year's call is interested in transformation, facade, growth, movement, generations, re/pavement, transmogrification and private/public space — "However, we will accept all submissions from Philadelphia artists." Up to three works, up to two images per work; time-based work goes in as a public YouTube or Vimeo link of ten minutes or less, and experimental and installation proposals are explicitly encouraged with an installation plan. The show runs December 10, 2026 to January 23, 2027, opening with a Second Thursday reception from 6 to 9pm and open Saturdays through the run. AUTOMAT is candid about the fee: "The $25 open call entry fee supports the general operation of AUTOMAT and the production of this show, which is otherwise funded by our artist members. We acknowledge the barriers that fees create for artist submissions" — artists who need it may select a $10 tier instead. Shipping both ways is the artist's cost; hand delivery is to Suite 105 on December 5. — Deadline: November 24, 2026. Fee: $25 ($10 reduced tier). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Anything You Can Imagine Is Real... — High School Senior Art Show · Pablo Center at the Confluence
item.description: A free show at Pablo Center at the Confluence for graduating high school seniors across the Chippewa Valley, and an unusually concrete first break: the first thirty submissions each receive a $250 cash stipend, additional cash prizes (sponsored by Cohen Law) go to the top three pieces, and selected work hangs in the Center's Foust Gallery. Pablo Center asks for whatever the senior year produced — "Whether your work is bold, thought-provoking, personal, or completely unexpected" — and the venue's exhibitions programme takes "original works of all mediums and styles", with no medium excluded, so photographic work is as eligible as anything else. Submission is by email to the visual arts coordinator and the call runs from 1 November to the 1 February deadline. The exhibition is on view 22 February to 19 April, with an artist reception and awards on 12 March, 5-7pm, in the Robert Manz Green Room. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $250 stipend + Cash prizes + Exhibition.

item.title: Pure Macro & Close-Up Photography Awards 2027
item.description: Pure Photography Awards' macro and close-up award, open worldwide and deliberately pitched at anyone who has looked closer — "You don't need to be a professional photographer to enter. You don't even need to call yourself a photographer." Insects, flowers, plants, textures, patterns, water, everyday objects and the smallest details of the natural world are all in scope, shot with a dedicated macro rig, a standard camera or a phone; a macro lens is not required. The Macro & Close-Up Photographer of the Year receives a US$500 cash prize and the official trophy, and winners, placed photographers and finalists are exhibited at the Pure Photography Awards exhibition in India, interviewed on the organisation's own site and carried through its press channels. Judging is by Marit van Ekelenburg, an OM SYSTEM Ambassador and Dutch macro photographer. Two rules carry weight here: AI-generated or AI-altered photographs are not accepted, though normal editing and focus stacking are allowed, and any photograph made by killing, harming, drugging, freezing, restraining or deliberately distressing an animal or insect is strictly refused. RAW or supporting files may be requested to verify any shortlisted or winning photograph. Copyright remains entirely with the entrant, and no further fees are charged after submission or selection. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: $17–$80 by image count. Prize: US$500 + Trophy + Exhibition.

item.title: Pure Portrait Photography Awards 2027
item.description: The inaugural portrait award from Pure Photography Awards, the platform built by Pure Street Photography's founders Dimpy Bhalotia and Kamal Kumaar Rao, and judged by Nick Brandt — whose On This Earth, Inherit the Dust, This Empty World and The Day May Break are among the most widely exhibited portrait-based photographic series of the last twenty years. The call treats a portrait as a study of identity, emotion, character and presence rather than a likeness: candid or directed, minimalist or elaborate, documentary or conceptual, studio, home, street or natural environment, in colour or black and white, and self-portraits are eligible. The Portrait Photographer of the Year takes a US$500 cash prize and the official trophy; winners, first, second and third places and finalists are all exhibited at the Pure Photography Awards exhibition in India, interviewed on the organisation's own site and carried through its press channels — the founders' previous Awards exhibition at the Jehangir Art Gallery in Mumbai drew more than 25,000 visitors over six days. Open worldwide to professionals and amateurs, shot on any camera or mobile device. AI-generated photographs are strictly not accepted. Copyright remains entirely with the photographer, and the organisers state that no further fees are charged after submission or selection. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: $17–$80 by image count. Prize: US$500 + Trophy + Exhibition.

item.title: Pure Street Photography Awards 2027
item.description: An international award given exclusively to street photography, run by the platform founded by photographers and curators Dimpy Bhalotia and Kamal Kumaar Rao. The 2027 edition is judged in three categories — Colour, Black & White and Animal — each with its own submission route and its own Photographer of the Year. Each category winner receives a US$500 cash prize and the official Pure Street Photography trophy, with winners, placed photographers and finalists all exhibited at the Awards exhibition in India, interviewed on the organisation's own site and carried through its press channels. The exhibitions are a matter of record rather than a promise: the 2025 edition filled the Jehangir Art Gallery in Mumbai from 22 to 27 January 2026 with 147 award-winning and finalist prints from 33 countries and more than 25,000 visitors in six days, and the 2026 edition is set for Jawahar Kala Kendra in Jaipur with 166 photographs from 50 countries. Entry is open to professionals and amateurs alike, from any camera or phone. Editing is held to exposure, contrast, tone, colour, crop and noise reduction — compositing, object removal, sky replacement and any generative AI are prohibited. Copyright stays with the photographer, selected work is used only for the Awards' own promotion, exhibitions and press, and nothing is printed in a book, zine or catalogue without written consent. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: $17–$80 by image count. Prize: US$500 + Trophy + Exhibition.

item.title: Cosmic Pop · Arts Alpharetta
item.description: Juried spring exhibition at the Alpharetta Arts Center, presented by Arts Alpharetta in partnership with the City of Alpharetta Cultural Services. Cosmic Pop asks for work celebrating bold colour, expressive linework and the imaginative spirit of Peter Max, whose own retrospective is shown alongside the selected exhibition — vibrant palettes, cosmic themes, pop-psychedelic energy, or a modern reading of that style in the artist's own terms. The organisers are explicit that this is not an imitation show: work must be original in concept, composition and execution and must not copy Max. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside drawing, painting, mixed media, printmaking, sculpture, kinetic art, ceramics, fiber and folk art. Artists 18 and over may submit up to three works at $15 per entry, one artwork per entry; reproductions of original works and pieces previously shown in the Arts Center's main gallery are not eligible. Accepted work must arrive gallery-ready, wired and ready to hang. The show runs March 10 to May 1, 2027, with a reception on Friday, March 12, 5-7pm. — Deadline: February 6, 2027. Fee: $15 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Counter-Memory — January 2027 Open Call · Thirdplat
item.description: Thirdplat's free monthly open call for January 2027 is about the histories that never reach an archive. Its own opening: "A family photograph survives, but nobody remembers every face. A building disappears, while its rooms remain familiar to someone who once lived there. Such memories rarely enter an official archive, yet they can change how we understand the past." The brief asks whose experiences are preserved and whose are left out — public monuments, colonial collections and digital archives all involve decisions about what deserves to remain, and personal accounts may challenge those decisions even though memory itself can be "incomplete, contradictory or difficult to trust". It invites work that approaches the past through its gaps and disagreements: returning to a family album, following an overlooked local history, working with inherited materials, or reconstructing a place from recollection, and it is interested in "how a work can recover an experience, question a record or hold conflicting memories together without forcing them to agree". Photography is named outright among the welcomed forms, alongside moving image, writing, craft, painting, performance, sound, design, installation and interdisciplinary practice. This is publication rather than competition: Thirdplat is an independent online platform that publishes accepted work directly into a permanent public archive with an individual page and artist credit, and selected works may be featured on its social channels and newsletter; the Terms of Use state that "Submission is free" and that "No payment, prize, commission or commercial agreement is created by submitting". Registered artists can also build a free artist profile and portfolio. Submitting runs through a Thirdplat account, and the Terms set the only entry bar: "You must be at least 18 years old to create an account or submit work through Thirdplat." Submissions close 31 January 2027. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: REFLECTION: AI AND US — December 2026 Open Call · Thirdplat
item.description: Thirdplat's free monthly open call for December 2026 treats artificial intelligence as a mirror rather than a subject in itself: "REFLECTION: AI AND US is not simply a theme about artificial intelligence, but an inquiry into what it reveals about the people who create, use and live alongside it." The platform's framing is that every generated image, sentence, voice and film begins with traces of human knowledge and work — "Like an echo, AI repeats and rearranges what we have already made. Like a mirror, it returns our imagination together with our habits, prejudices, desires and fears" — and it names the questions it wants work to take on: authorship, originality, labour, consent and trust, and "Who creates a work when human intention meets machine generation?" Submissions may use AI as a creative tool or as a subject, and equally may "observe, question, challenge, resist or reimagine it". Photography is named outright among the welcomed forms, alongside moving image, writing, craft, sound, performance and cross-disciplinary work. This is publication rather than competition: Thirdplat is an independent online platform that publishes accepted work directly into a permanent public archive with an individual page and artist credit, and its Terms of Use state plainly that "Submission is free" and that "No payment, prize, commission or commercial agreement is created by submitting". Thirteen works are already published under this theme. Submitting runs through a Thirdplat account, and the Terms set the only entry bar: "You must be at least 18 years old to create an account or submit work through Thirdplat." Submissions close 31 December 2026; the January 2027 theme (Counter-Memory) is open alongside it. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 77: All About Me, Using Metaphors to Explore Identity
item.description: UK-based independent online zine, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, calling for visual art and writing on identity told through metaphor. The brief asks artists to look past the literal self-portrait and consider how objects, animals, landscapes, colours, patterns, symbols and everyday things might stand in for different parts of who they are — "show us what represents you" — and says the work may be playful, reflective, abstract, humorous, challenging or deeply personal, since identity is layered and constantly evolving. Media are open and photography is named explicitly alongside painting, drawing and illustration, digital art, sculpture and 3D work, textiles, collage and mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, installation and conceptual art; writers may send short stories, essays, poetry, experimental and cross-genre work. Open internationally to artists and writers at any stage, including students, recent graduates and the self-taught — the editors say they are interested in ideas and practices rather than credentials. Free to enter and free if selected. Submit one to three artworks with title, year, medium, dimensions and a statement explaining the metaphor behind the work; a public Instagram handle is a stated requirement, because selected work is tagged across the zine's 11,000-follower platform, and the editors say they will not select artists without one. Fully AI-generated work is excluded: the work "must be resolved, not generated by AI". There is no cash prize and no payment to artists — selected works appear in a curated online group exhibition on haus-a-rest.com and in the December issue, typically online for about six months, and artists retain all rights. — Deadline: November 27, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Confluence Gallery 2027-2028 Exhibition Proposals · Artistry Theater and Visual Arts
item.description: A free call for exhibition proposals from Artistry and the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge, whose Confluence Gallery sits inside the Refuge's Education and Visitor Center in Bloomington. The Refuge runs to more than 14,000 acres along 70 miles of the Minnesota River, and the gallery exists as a conduit between that landscape and the communities around it, so proposals are asked to focus on nature, natural elements, ecology, conservation or the beauty of the Minnesota River Valley. Minnesota-resident artists aged 18 and over working in any visual medium may propose a show for the 2027 or 2028 programme year; solo exhibitions are the likely outcome, though two artists may be paired. Each selected artist also presents a workshop, artist talk or other engagement event, developed with Artistry and Refuge staff. Each selected artist receives a $300 stipend. A proposal is ten images, work details and a statement of 1,000 characters or less, reviewed by a curatorial panel on relevance to the gallery's mission, artistic excellence, originality and technical skill. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $300 stipend + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Paint Rock Forest Artist Residency 2027 — The Moving Forest · Paint Rock Research Center
item.description: A free residency on a 4,000-acre forest preserve in the Paint Rock Valley of Jackson County, Alabama, where scientists study one of North America's richest concentrations of deciduous forest, cave and aquatic biodiversity. Twelve Alabama-based artists and musicians will be hosted in cohorts of three or four for a Thursday-to-Sunday stay at the Paint Rock Research Center, working alongside researchers on forest dynamics, caves, salamanders, river mussels and prescribed-fire recovery, with guided excursions into private land including The Nature Conservancy's Sharp-Bingham Mountain Preserve. Photographers are named first among the media invited. The 2027 cohort is led by artists and educators from the Department of Art + Design at Jacksonville State University; residents receive a $250 honorarium, show in a month-long group exhibition at the Gadsden Museum of Art in January 2028, and give a talk or workshop at JSU. Lodging is in the preserve's Red House; a panel of five jurors selects on merit and fit with the programme's themes. — Deadline: January 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: $250 honorarium + Group exhibition.

item.title: Call for L.A. Artists: Digital Art, Photography and Video · Los Angeles Center for Digital Art
item.description: A free open call from the Los Angeles Center for Digital Art, the downtown LA gallery founded in 2004 that has worked with curators from MoCA, LACMA and the Hammer Museum. Director and curator Rex Bruce selects digital stills, photography and short looping video art by L.A.-area artists for a gallery show running January 7-30, 2027, with a reception on opening night. The brief is deliberately unfashionable: academic, experimental, underground and outsider work is encouraged, well-conceived AI is welcome, and the gallery states plainly that this is not a venue for fashion, popular music, narrative entertainment, craft or commerce. Entry is free, registration is online only, three images per entry and there is no limit on the number of entries. — Deadline: December 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Small Works Exhibition & Sale · Medford Arts Center
item.description: The Medford Arts Center, a community arts centre at 8 North Main Street in Medford, New Jersey, closes its 2026 exhibition year with Small Works, an all-media show of pieces twelve inches or under on every side, frame excluded. The organisers are unusually plain about how selection works and it is worth reading before entering: this show is "juried for Awards only" and "ALL works will be included in the online exhibit", so entry buys a place in the online show and in the printed brochure and YouTube video, while the jurying decides the prizes rather than who gets in. Artists who can hand-deliver also have the option of having their pieces displayed physically in the gallery in Medford. The juror is Gwynn Di Pilla and the show is chaired by Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Photography is named in the eligibility line itself - the call is "OPENED TO - Artists & Photographers, 18 years and older" - and the centre has run a dedicated photography exhibition, Looking Through the Lens, in the same year. Cash awards go to first, second and third place with three honourable mentions; the amounts are not published in the prospectus. Up to five pieces may be entered at 30 dollars for the first and 10 for each additional, or 20 and 10 for members of the centre, all non-refundable. Work must be original and conceived and signed by the artist, must not have been shown at the centre before, and must be family friendly. Every piece must be for sale: the centre takes a 30 per cent commission, collects sales tax, notifies the artist of a sale, and the artist then ships the sold work to the buyer, so entrants are told to price work to cover shipping and not to add extra shipping charges except for buyers outside their own country. Entry images should exclude frame and mat, be cropped to the edge of the image, 300 dpi and under 5 MB. The deadline is midnight on Monday 30 November 2026; the awards reception is on Friday 4 December from 6 to 8pm, awards and the exhibit go online on Saturday 5 December, and the exhibition runs to 7 January 2027. The centre states that work is handled with all possible care but that it will not be held responsible for loss or damage from any cause. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $30 first work ($20 members), $10 each additional. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 2027/28 Place-Based Artist Residencies · Open AIR
item.description: Open AIR is a Missoula-based non-profit that runs place-based artist residencies across Montana, partly funded by the Montana Arts Council and four family foundations, and it is taking applications for its 2027/28 cycle of residencies the organisers bill as four to six weeks long, though the published session dates run from three weeks in the Selway Bitterroot wilderness to six in Butte. Rather than a single studio building, the programme places artists at specific sites - the published 2027/28 list is Garden City Harvest, Home ReSource, the Daly Mansion, the Flathead Lake Biological Station, Rocky Mountain Gardens, Philipsburg, the spectrUM science museum, the Selway Bitterroot Frank Church wilderness, Missoula Public Library, Butte and a natural-history residency run with the Montana Natural History Center and the University of Montana's zoology museum - and asks them to make work in relation to that place: "artists can connect with the individuals stewarding that site and develop unique work in relation to the place they are in residence". Applicants choose between three and five sites from the published list, which is split into general residency sites and a separate set of Indigenous residency opportunities sharing the same deadline: a five-site summer cohort (American Prairie, the Kingsley History Project, the Montana Heritage Center, the Moon-Randolph Homestead, Five Valleys Land Trust) and a fall residency at the CSKT Bison Range, both open to Indigenous artists only. There is no charge to take part once selected. Open AIR provides studio space at the site, housing for every artist travelling from out of town, community engagement and professional-development opportunities including exhibitions and artist talks, a listing and promotion on its own channels, and a modest stipend of 35 US dollars for every day of the residency; artists pay their own travel and food. In return, residents join weekly check-ins, take part in community engagement such as studio visits, talks, performances or workshops shaped around their own practice, share their process in photographs and recorded talks, and contribute one piece of digital content or artwork to the organisation's collection as an educational resource - a physical object is optional, not required. Artists in Missoula also get access to community resources including the Montana Natural History Center, Home ReSource, Free Cycles, the MCAT Media Center, MUD Missoula, Missoula Public Library and the University of Montana. The call is open to artists of all disciplines living and working in the United States and abroad, aged 18 and over, at any career stage, and students may apply for a residency during a break; Indigenous artists and members of other under-represented groups are explicitly encouraged. Photography is well represented in the programme's own history: past cohorts list Jordan Lefler and Logan Lefler (photographer/filmmaker) and Forest Woodward (photographer) at the CSKT Bison Range, and the Belgian photographer and visual artist Catherine Lemblé in Missoula. Applications cost 30 dollars for up to three sites and 10 dollars for each additional site, and the organisers waive the fee on request if it is a barrier. The application asks for five to ten work samples (or adequate samples for non-visual media, no file over 1 GB), a 100-word bio, a 500-word description of your creative practice, a creative-practice resume, responses on why your chosen sites fit your interests, and optionally a workshop idea for the community. A team of unnamed jurors selects on merit, excellence and fit to site, reading work samples alongside the site commentary; finalists are interviewed by phone. The deadline is 11:59 pm MST on Monday 30 November 2026 and everyone is notified by the end of March 2027. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $30 for up to 3 sites, $10 each additional site. Prize: 4–6 week residency + $35/day stipend.

item.title: Variations 2027 · Marblehead Arts Association
item.description: The Marblehead Arts Association, a 501(c)(3) non-profit housed in the historic 1728 mansion at 8 Hooper Street in Marblehead, Massachusetts, invites "artists, both MAA members and non-members, from across the country" to its national juried exhibit Variations 2027, an eight-week show running 24 April to 19 June 2027. Work is juried in three categories and judged for prizes in each of them, and photography is one: the organiser's category list reads "Photography - Film, Digital (the artist must make the image)", alongside Fine Art (painting, drawing, printmaking, 2-D mixed media, digital art) and 3D (sculpture, crafts, jewelry, fabric, paper). Cash prizes of $1,000, $250 and $100 are awarded in each category, so a photographer competes against photographers for the $1,000, and the awards are presented at the opening reception on Sunday 25 April 2027. All three judges are named on the call page: the painter, sculptor and printmaker Jennifer Day (MFA, University of Pennsylvania, under Neil Welliver) judges Fine Art; Jim Fitts - a photographer, teacher and curator of more than 45 years, former Executive Director of the Photographic Resource Center at Boston University, curator of photography exhibitions for the PRC/MIT Gallery and a reviewer for Photolucida, FotoFest and the New England Portfolio Reviews - judges Photography; and Paula Bradstreet Richter, a curator specialising in fashion, textiles and New England decorative arts, judges 3D. The organiser states that acceptance and prize decisions are the judges' alone and that no one associated with the association takes part in either process. Entry is through CaFE at $35 for a first entry plus $10 for each additional work, up to three works, with a $10 discount for current MAA members on their first entry at checkout and no refunds after payment. Submission images must be JPEGs cropped to remove backgrounds, under 5 MB, at least 100 dpi, with the longest side no more than 1,400 pixels. The photography rules bar synthetic imagery: "Composite images are acceptable. All parts of the image must be created photographically by the artist. Computer-generated or AI subject is not allowed." Submissions opened on 14 November 2026 and close on 22 February 2027; the jury's decisions are emailed on 15 March 2027 and accepted work must arrive - hand-delivered or shipped to the gallery in Marblehead - by 11 April 2027, with local pick-up from 20 June and a packing and shipping week of 21 to 25 June. Artists under 18 need an adult sponsor; no residency or nationality bar is published. Accepted work must remain hanging until the exhibit closes unless it sells, and accepted 2-D work has to arrive framed and wired for the gallery's Walker rod system. The association keeps 40 per cent of any sale and pays the artist 60 per cent, on sales during the show and for 30 days after it closes, and it takes no responsibility for work lost or damaged in transit, asking artists to insure and track their shipments and to enclose a pre-paid return label. Work accepted or exhibited in the 2023, 2024, 2025 or 2026 Variations shows cannot be entered again. The MAA has exhibited work from across New England in the seven galleries of its mansion for over a century. — Deadline: February 22, 2027. Fee: $35 first entry, $10 each additional work; $10 MAA member discount. Prize: $1,000 cash + Exhibition.

item.title: AAP Magazine #63 Colors · All About Photo
item.description: The 63rd printed issue of AAP Magazine takes Colors as its theme. The editors open with the premise that "life is a stream of colors" - red, blue, yellow and all the possible combinations between those primaries, black and white not forgotten - and ask for images "both where colors may not just influence the pictures, but where it may also be the subject solely". The call is explicitly open to any colour interpretation and names photojournalism, street, artistic, portrait, nude, landscape, nature, wildlife, urban, architecture, fashion, fine art and documentary photography as eligible approaches. What the magazine wants is a body of work rather than one-off frames: the brief asks "preferably a cohesive body of work or portfolio", and the judging runs in two passes - photographs are scored individually from 1 to 5 in a first round, then read as a unified group as they could be published in the issue. Work already published in AAP Magazine cannot be entered again. Twenty-five photographers are selected: $500 for first place with an exclusive interview, $300 for second and $200 for third, and the ranks from 4 to 25 are finalists. Every one of the 25 is published in AAP Magazine Volume 63: Colors, receives a free copy of the printed issue, which is sold and distributed through Blurb, and keeps a permanent place in the Winners Gallery on all-about-photo.com. The single juror is Sandrine Hermand-Grisel, the photographer, curator and editor who co-founded All About Photo with her husband in 2013 and is editor-in-chief of AAP Magazine. Entry costs $35 for the first three images and $5 for each additional image, with an early rate of $30 for the first three valid through 3 December 2026; up to 40 images may be entered, so a full 40-image entry costs $220 at the regular rate. Files are JPEG, 72 dpi, grayscale or RGB, flattened, under 2 MB, longest dimension between 200 and 1,200 pixels, no watermarks. Submission works through an account on the All About Photo website: register, upload to your gallery, then pay - and the organisers warn in capitals that an entry cannot be edited and images cannot be added once payment has been processed. The FAQ puts eligibility at "all individuals age 18 and older... professional and amateur photographers alike", while the binding Rules page sets the bar at the age of majority in the entrant's own jurisdiction and adds that the competition is void where prohibited and governed by the laws of California, so check your own jurisdiction. The published schedule is: competition opens 14 November 2026, closes 15 December 2026, judging runs 19 December 2026 to 15 January 2027, and winners are notified by email around 30 January 2027, with the winning images online after that date. Photographers retain full copyright in every entry, and cash prizes are paid by wire transfer with any foreign-currency transfer fees deducted from the winning amount. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 images ($30 until Dec 3), $5 each additional. Prize: $500/$300/$200 + Publication.

item.title: 101 Art Book: Garden Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: Arts to Hearts Project's 101 Art Book series reaches its sixteenth volume with the Garden Edition, a hardcover publication built around a single theme interpreted by 101 artists from around the world. The series began in 2023 and has published fifteen editions and more than 1,300 artists so far, with volumes on Photography, Food, Collage, Landscape, Abstract, Portrait, Animal, Floral, Nature, Dogs, Pattern, Colors, Faces and Texture; this one asks for work drawn from the natural world. The organisers frame a garden as more than a place where things grow - a world of colours, forms, patterns, textures, movement and transformation that can be found in a single flower, the shape of a leaf, the flight of a butterfly, an overgrown landscape or an imagined world filled with life - and they open the theme to each artist's own reading of it. Flowers, plants, trees, leaves, grass, fruits, seeds, insects, butterflies and birds are all named, as are landscapes, forests, wild gardens, botanical forms and seasonal change, and so is the unexpected beauty of weeds, tangled branches, fallen leaves and decaying flowers; symbolic, conceptual and wholly abstract interpretations are explicitly welcome. Photography is named twice in the call's own words - nature photography sits in the list of eligible work, and the FAQ answers a photographer directly: work exploring flowers, plants, landscapes, wildlife, botanical details and natural patterns is eligible. AI-generated artwork is not. Entry is open worldwide to artists 18 and over at any career stage, including self-taught and unrepresented artists, with no requirement of formal art education, gallery representation or exhibition history, and individual artists only. The fee is a tiered image ladder: 21 US dollars for one image, 35 for three, 47 for five, 62 for ten and 100 for twenty, with a separate optional 22-dollar add-on for a virtual studio-visit interview published on the organisation's website if selected, which is not required to enter. Every selected artist is published in the book alongside the other hundred and receives an official certificate of recognition; the book also carries interviews with the guest curator, collectors, galleries, industry figures and the cover artist, and selected artists are included in the publication's marketing campaign across an audience the organisation puts at over 190,000. One artist receives a 500 US dollar cash award, a four-page spread and a trophy. The books are produced as premium hardcovers and sold at 120 dollars each, distributed through Amazon and Barnes & Noble. Applications close on 13 December 2026; the organisers aim to announce results within ten days and commit to announcing them within three weeks of the deadline, with the clock restarting if the deadline is extended. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: $21–$100. Prize: $500 + Publication + 4-page feature.

item.title: Tails, Scales, & Toe-beans · Buckham Gallery
item.description: Buckham Gallery in Flint, Michigan - the exhibiting arm of Buckham Fine Arts Project, a 501(c)(3) non-profit founded in 1984 - is taking entries for Tails, Scales, & Toe-beans, a national juried exhibition built on Freud's uncanny. The gallery quotes his term umheimlich, or un-home-like, which described the sensation of being uncomfortably unfamiliar, and asks for artwork that dares to explore the world of the uncomfortably unfamiliar through inventive creatures and uncanny monsters. All media are accepted and the theme is open to interpretation: the open media are two-dimensional, three-dimensional and video work, so photography is eligible alongside everything else, and all work must be original in concept - the gallery excludes both reproductions and AI-created work. Unusually for a fee-charging open call, the gallery pays the artist as well as charging them: every artist selected for the exhibition receives a 50 US dollar stipend towards shipping, which the gallery openly acknowledges may not cover the full cost of sending work and having it returned, and stipend cheques are posted within five business days of the opening once the work has arrived in good condition. Entry costs 25 dollars for one to three works, paid by card or PayPal through a link that arrives in the confirmation message after the form is submitted, and the fee is non-refundable; members of the Buckham Arts Collective may enter free of charge, though they do not receive the shipping stipend. Entrants must be 18 or over and resident in the USA. Applications go through a Google form linked from the gallery's own call page by 21 November 2026, and every entrant is told the outcome by 5 December 2026; selected artists then complete a consignment agreement and must get their work to the gallery between 16 and 22 December 2026, handling packing, shipping and return shipping, or dropping off and collecting in person. The exhibition itself runs 8 to 30 January 2027 at the gallery in Flint: the submission form states that the Tails, Scales, and Toe-beans exhibition will be held January 8 - January 30, 2027, and the gallery's published 2026-2027 season carries an unnamed National Juried Exhibition in that same 8 to 30 January slot. One sentence on the call page is stale and should be read as such - it places an Abstraction exhibition at 9 to 30 January 2027, while Abstraction is in fact the juried show hanging now, 13 November to 19 December 2026, on the gallery's own front page and in its published season; the deadline, the notification date and the delivery window are identical on every surface. Selection is by blind review from the digital files, judged on whether the work presents perspectives not already represented in other area venues, is made to high technical and professional standards, and makes a unique statement in its chosen discipline or medium. The gallery's jury and presentation guidelines also bind selected work: it must arrive ready to hang with D-ring or eye-hook hardware and braided picture wire rated to the weight, no sawtooth or clip hangers, works on paper matted under glass or plexiglas unless the exhibition committee approves another approach, finished edges on unframed gallery-wrapped canvases, artist-supplied A/V equipment for video, and anything not claimed within 30 days of the exhibition's end becomes the property of Buckham Gallery. Work may be offered for sale but does not have to be; artists set their own retail prices, and the gallery takes a 35 per cent commission on anything sold, leaving 65 per cent to the artist, and covers card processing fees out of its own share. Buckham's funders include the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation, the Michigan Arts and Culture Council, the National Endowment for the Arts and the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Group exhibition.
