item.title: COSMOS · Photopolis Festival
item.description: Photopolis Festival, the international photography and film festival held each year in Agrinio in western Greece since 2019, is assembling a group photographic exhibition called COSMOS for April 2027 as part of its pre-festival programme. The theme is deliberately wide: the festival invites photographers to look at the world around them and beyond it, naming the universe, nature, the human being, matter, relationships, harmony and chaos, and the visible and invisible connections that make up our existence as possible starting points for different photographic readings. Two photographers assess the proposals - Eleni Mouzakiti and Lila Zotou. Submitting is free. Photographers send one to three high-resolution photographs, of which at most one may be selected, and those whose work is chosen then pay 50 euros as a contribution to the costs of mounting the show, which the festival says covers the printing of the photographs, the curation and the organisational expenses. Files must be printable quality - the long edge at least 4000 pixels at 240 dpi - named with the photographer's name in Latin characters followed by 1, 2 or 3, and sent through WeTransfer or another cloud service rather than attached directly, together with a Word file giving name, city, telephone, email and Instagram handle if there is one. The festival sends a confirmation within 48 hours and asks anyone who does not receive it to get in touch. Photographs must not be created with AI technology. Entrants grant the organisers the right to publish and exhibit the work and to post it on social media to promote the festival, always with the photographer's name credited and with no fee due for that use; copyright stays with the photographer, and the festival states that the prints will be destroyed after the exhibition closes. Selected photographers are notified by email. The call closes on 31 December 2026. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free (€50 if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Shenandoah National Park Artist in Residence
item.description: Shenandoah National Park gives one artist at a time three weeks in the Blue Ridge with a rustic, furnished house to themselves, and photographers are among the disciplines it names: the park's CaFE listing runs them in with writers, composers, painters, sculptors, needleworkers and poets, while the park's own page says simply that artists of all disciplines are encouraged to apply. Six residency windows are offered across 2027 - 27 April to 18 May, 1 to 22 June, 29 June to 20 July, 27 July to 17 August, 7 to 28 September and 7 to 28 October - and the park asks applicants to be ready to work largely independently in a semi-remote setting where the cellular signal is very limited, though Wi-Fi reaches the house. The residency pays a 1,200 US dollar stipend plus up to 100 dollars for materials used in public programming, and is funded by a donation from the Shenandoah National Park Trust. In return the resident presents at least two public programs during the stay and donates one original work to the Trust within six months; the park may show donated work in local galleries, visitor centres and community outreach. The park's own account of the programme makes clear that photography is a real part of it: the 2026 cohort of seven included a night photographer who gave a public programme on painting with light at Big Meadows. Practical conditions matter here. Artists must provide their own art supplies and must have their own transport to and within the park for the whole residency, and proposals or finished works may not manipulate or disturb the park's natural and cultural landscape except as the Superintendent's Compendium allows. The house is for the artist alone: joint applications from collaborating artists are considered, but family members, friends and partners may not stay in it. The application is a single submission through CaFE with a 5 dollar fee and up to five files - still images, audio or video, five in total, of which at least two work samples are required - plus answers to several questions, a resume, the applicant's availability and a reference contact; the park asks for demonstrated proficiency and a strong commitment to the chosen medium, and applicants must be at least 18. One practical note on where to apply: the park's own page has not been updated for this round, still presenting the 2026 residents and an email alert for when applications are announced, so the CaFE listing is the live application. The published timeline runs from a panel review between 13 January and 14 February 2027, through notice of non-selection or an interview request on 19 February and finalist interviews from 22 February to 5 March, to decisions shared with interviewed applicants on 22 March 2027. Applications close at 11:59pm Eastern on 12 January 2027, a deadline the park states it will not extend under any circumstances. — Deadline: January 12, 2027. Fee: $5. Prize: $1,200 stipend + 3-week residency.

item.title: P5: Photo Poetry Pamphlet Series — Volumes 5 and 6 · Photoworks
item.description: Photoworks, the Brighton-based charity with a national remit for photography in England, is looking for two projects to become volumes 5 and 6 of P5, its photo-poetry pamphlet series developed with David Solo and designed by the studio Jane & Jeremy. The series launched in 2025; its first four volumes each pair photography with poetry on the page, and the two new volumes are scheduled to launch in spring 2027. What Photoworks wants is existing, unpublished work in which text and image genuinely act on each other: the call states it is interested in projects where the relationship between the two goes beyond illustration or caption, and submissions are assessed on the strength of both the photography and the writing, how they combine to create layered meanings and further readings, and how the work would translate into the pamphlet form through sequencing, layout and visual presentation. Artists working across photography and poetry may apply individually or collaboratively, and an applicant must be the creator or co-creator of both the photographs and the text, with everything original and the text predominantly in English. Each of the two selected pamphlets is produced in full colour at roughly 6 x 9 inches, 32 to 48 pages, in what the organisation calls a substantial print run, and sold through the Photoworks online shop, selected stockists and related events. Each selected project carries a GBP 1,000 artist fee, 15 complimentary copies, the chance to develop the publication with Jane & Jeremy, and promotion and programming support. Entry is free: the Microsoft Forms application has eight questions and no payment step. It asks for artist name or names, a contact email address, city and country of residence, a biography of 200 words or less per artist, a project description of 600 words or less, a 400-word answer on why the work suits publication in the series, and a link to a draft manuscript or example of the proposed work hosted on a file-sharing service with viewing permission set to anyone with the link - Photoworks states it cannot consider submissions it cannot open. Work that is not yet finished is allowed if the link shows at least 12 pages of images and text and the form gives an estimated completion date. The call is explicitly international and open to artists at all career stages regardless of experience, affiliation or status; applicants must be 18 or over. An online information session with the Photoworks team, David Solo and Siddharth Khajuria, a previous P5 awardee, runs on Wednesday 2 December from 4pm to 5pm and is booked through Eventbrite. The deadline is midnight GMT on Wednesday 27 January 2027. — Deadline: January 27, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + Publication.

item.title: All Abstraction · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: Site:Brooklyn's online juried exhibition on non-representational art, from geometric precision to gestural spontaneity and from material experimentation to digital invention — work that treats abstraction as method, philosophy or artistic language, whether aiming at conceptual clarity, engaging culturally specific practices or pushing into unclassifiable territory. The gallery states it welcomes all media, naming painting, sculpture, collage, textile and photography, and the call is open to all artists 18 and over internationally. The juror is Claudia Ross, a writer based in Los Angeles who contributes art criticism, interviews and essays to ArtReview, Artforum, Frieze, Hyperallergic, New York Review of Architecture, BOMB and The Creative Independent. Submit 3 to 12 images of original work, measured in imperial dimensions, with up to 3 video samples allowed inside a 15-sample total; the fee is $26 for three images and $10 for each additional image, non-refundable. All work must be priced for sale and must stay available for the run, with artists retaining a 60% commission on exhibition sales; accepted artists upload high-resolution files. The call was announced 12 November 2026, entries close 4 January 2027 at 11:59pm PT, notification letters go out 13 January 2027 and the exhibition is online 22 January – 22 February 2027. The gallery's requirement block prints that same cutoff as 11:59pm MT, which is 10:59pm PT; the entry system's own localised deadline reads 11:59 p.m. PST, so the safe plan is the earlier of the two. Site:Brooklyn has moved its programme online, running open-call exhibitions selected by guest jurors alongside solo features and spotlights. — Deadline: January 4, 2027. Fee: $26 (3 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: ZELZAL 004 — The Beauty of the Margins
item.description: ZELZAL is an independent bilingual (EN/AR) print publication of art and fashion that publishes artists from the Global South and its diasporas, designed and printed in the UAE and sold as numbered, collectible books; the publication says its 003 edition, Formation, sold out in 24 hours. Issue 004, The Beauty of the Margins / جمال الهامش, is an open call for image makers — photographers and directors — from the Global South and its diasporas, asking for "your culture, seen from inside": living traditions, contemporary scenes, the people around you, and "the scenes, communities and rituals that live on the margins". Any subject, "as long as it's yours". Send either a photo series of 8 to 15 images from one series, or a film or video of up to five minutes (short documentary, music video, fashion film or video art, with up to five stills), plus a statement of about 150 words in English, Arabic or French; the form also asks where and when the work was shot and how you are part of the scene you photographed. Only unpublished work qualifies — not yet shared publicly on social media or in any other publication, though private or unlisted links are fine — and a finished work or a project in progress are both welcome. Entry is free and photographers keep their copyright; selected image makers agree that ZELZAL prints the work and shares it, credited, to promote the issue, and the organisers state that they print images whole, with no crops. The deadline is Tuesday 1 December 2026 at 23:59 Dubai time (GMT+4); selected image makers are notified in mid-December 2026, and final files — TIFF or maximum-quality JPEG at 3,500 px or more on the long side, or a film's full-resolution master plus stills for print — are due by Monday 4 January 2027. Images upload directly on the call page, and when that upload space fills the organisers point applicants to a backup Google Form at forms.gle/J2FJc8xczVd3uqbA9 carrying the same questions and the same deadline. AI is barred: "No AI-generated images or footage", and the entrant's declaration confirms that no image or footage "is AI-generated or AI-altered beyond normal editing". No jurors are named on any ZELZAL surface. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Slide Night 2026 · Luxembourg Streetphoto Collective
item.description: The Luxembourg Streetphoto Collective — Street Photography Luxembourg a.s.b.l., based at 3 Place des Rotondes in Luxembourg City, organiser of the Light Leaks Festival and of the Streets Unplugged podcast, and described in its own Instagram bio as a non-profit organisation — runs Slide Night as its annual projection evening at Rotondes. The 2026 announcement invites "street and documentary photographers to submit their work" and states that "selected photographs will be projected on the big screen on 9 December 2026", with a submission deadline of 25 November 2026. Asked in the comments what the prize was, the collective answered from its own account: "First price gets to exhibit during the Light Leaks Festival in May 2027" — so the winning photographer carries over into the collective's own festival exhibition. THIS YEAR'S RULES ARE ON THE ENTRY FORM, NOT THE WEBSITE: streetphoto.lu still reads "Streetphoto.lu is under reconstruction!" and its newest Slide Night page is the 2025 edition, but the Google Form linked from the collective's Instagram bio as "SlideNight2026" is live and titled SLIDE NIGHT SUBMISSIONS 2026, and it carries the 2026 terms in full. The evening runs 19:00–21:00 on 9 December 2026 at Plateforme / Rotondes. The deadline is 25 November 2026 at 23:59 and the jury replies on 1 December. Work must fall under street or documentary photography, must be original and made by the submitting photographer, and may have been taken anywhere in the world. The entry itself is a slideshow that must include music and run no longer than three minutes, uploaded as a high-quality MP4, and selected photographers are required to be present on the night. The form asks for name, birthday, email, phone, Instagram handle and a title for the slideshow, and it records the name and email on your Google account when you upload the file — so you need to be signed in to Google to submit, which is also why the form is unreadable without an account. The collective's standing Slide Night terms and conditions require participants to be of legal age in their country or to have parental consent, state that late entries will not be accepted, leave ownership with the photographer while granting the collective a non-exclusive royalty-free licence to use the work for the event and related promotion, and are governed by Luxembourg law. No entry fee appears on the announcement, on those terms, or anywhere on the 2026 form, which has no payment step — that is the basis for the free fee stored here. The form says only that "our jury will curate all submissions"; no jurors are named. — Deadline: November 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Projection + Exhibition.

item.title: Young FORMAT27
item.description: FORMAT, the UK's leading festival of international photography, established in 2004 and run by QUAD in Derby, opens its strand for photographers aged 25 and under for the FORMAT27 Biennale. QUAD/FORMAT's Young Advocates and Photofusion's Young Curators — Photofusion is described by the call as "London's largest all-encompassing photography centre" — are "seeking photographs from children and young people, aged 25 years and under, to exhibit as part of the FORMAT27 Biennale in Derby and at Photofusion in London". The two young curatorial teams each curate a physical exhibition of selected works, one at QUAD in Derby and one at Photofusion in London, both shown during 2027; FORMAT27 itself runs across Derby venues from 11 March to 11 April 2027 on the festival theme of PLAY. The brief asks for your interpretation of PLAY and is explicit that no special equipment or experience is needed: "Use what you've got… There's no right or wrong way to do this, so enjoy yourself and feel free to experiment." It suggests thinking about angles and viewpoints, composition, shape, light and colour, abstract and conceptual readings of the theme, experimenting with new techniques and unconventional methods. SUBMISSION: up to five images with a short description of how the work responds to the theme, through the festival's Tally form; JPEG or JPG, each file no larger than 10 MB, named FIRSTNAME_AGE (the call's own example is AMY_22). Work selected but supplied at too low a print quality will be shown on a digital display instead, and depending on volume other submissions may be shown as a collage or on digital display. Teachers and lecturers submitting on behalf of students indicate this on the form. Under-18s must have their work submitted by a parent or legal guardian, and any image featuring a person under 18 needs a completed consent form, downloadable through the submission form, or the work cannot be exhibited; images of under-18s will not be used in promotional material. DEADLINE CAUTION: the call page prints two different dates — "Deadline for submissions: Sunday 13th December 2026" at the top and "Submission deadline: Sunday 6 December 2026" lower down. The submission form itself states Sunday 13 December 2026, which is the date stored here; if you want to be safe, submit by 6 December. Outcomes are announced in February 2027. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at QUAD, Derby and Photofusion, London.
